text:
Nils Lundkvist is the kind of defenseman whose value is easy to miss in the box score: no goals in 19 games, six assists, 13 shots. But Dallas takes 55% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on, five points better than without him, and his minutes have been climbing, past 20 a night in three of his last four games and 24 against Winnipeg.

That's in line with what Evolving-Hockey saw last season: 1.1 wins above replacement, 63rd among 215 defensemen, with most of it on defense and opponents getting fewer chances with him out there (86th percentile). Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds the other half of his game: 6.1 primary shot assists per 60, 88th percentile among defensemen. He moves it to the shooter rather than shooting it himself.

The 2018 first-rounder came to Dallas from the Rangers and has settled into a steady second- or third-pair role. Three assists in his last two games is the best stretch of his season. The goals will likely stay rare (his own chance rate is tiny), and that's fine. Watch the minutes; they tell you how much the Stars trust him.
